setup.words: A pipe, D = 20 mm, L = 300 mm (15 D) along +x from x = 0 (STEP in mm, built with OCP); a custom fluid with nu = 0.0002 m²/s and rho = 1 kg/m³, so Re = U D / nu = 100; a velocity inlet of 1 m/s normal to the face, a 0 Pa pressure outlet and a no-slip wall; laminar, steady (simpleFoam), Accurate numerics, residual targets 1e-6, at most 3000 iterations.

geometry.builder: pipe, D = 20 mm, L = 300 mm (15 D) along +x from x = 0

estimate.n_cells_note: an order of magnitude (1.3 to 1.4 times case 1's real meshes), not a prediction

setup.mesh_words: Hex-dominant at fineness 6 with an Inflate boundary layer of 4 layers, 1 mm in all, on the wall (automatic boundary layers off); 1 non-orthogonal corrector

rows.text: The run starts from rest; starting from potential flow shortens the start-up.

estimate.line: 3,000 iterations at most · ~23 minutes on 4 cores · Re ≈ 100

histories.label: U_x at the centreline probe at x = 12 D

quantities.label: Darcy friction factor × Re, developed part (x/D 10 to 13)

uncertainty.what: the slope's standard error and twice the cross-section's

quantities.how: f·Re = 2 D_eff² (−dp/dx) / (mu U_b): dp/dx the least-squares slope of the centreline pressure from Plot over path (0,0,0) to (0.3,0,0) m, 300 subdivisions, over x/D 10 to 13; U_b = Q / A and D_eff = sqrt(4 A / pi), Q the flow through the inlet and A the pipe's meshed cross-section, the mean of the inlet's and the outlet's mesh areas (all three from the run's monitors), since a meshed circle's area is not exactly pi D²/4

reference.citation: G. Hagen (1839), "Ueber die Bewegung des Wassers in engen cylindrischen Röhren", Ann. Phys. Chem. 46:423-442; J. L. M. Poiseuille (1840), C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 11:961-967, 1041-1048: the exact (Hagen-Poiseuille) solution of the Navier-Stokes equations for fully developed laminar pipe flow
reference.where: Darcy f = 64/Re (f = 0.640 at Re 100), i.e. -dp/dx = 32 mu U / D² = 16 Pa/m here
reference.conditions: fully developed, steady, Newtonian; Re = rho U D / mu with U the bulk (mean) speed; Re = 100

tolerance.note: the answer is exact, so only mesh error remains

quantities.detail: -dp/dx 15.8252 Pa/m from 60 samples (slope standard error 0.01 %, r² 0.999999); D_eff 19.995 mm, U_b 1.0000 m/s

quantities.label: Centreline speed / bulk speed, developed part (x/D 10 to 13)
quantities.how: the centre value u_c of a least-squares fit U_x = u_c + b r² (the developed profile's own form) to the cell values, not interpolated, of every cell whose centre lies in x/D 10 to 13 within R/2 of the axis, read from the run's saved U by the app's own volume loader (case_volume.load_volume, the code behind Plot over path), over U_b = Q / A (as for f·Re)

reference.citation: G. Hagen (1839), "Ueber die Bewegung des Wassers in engen cylindrischen Röhren", Ann. Phys. Chem. 46:423-442; J. L. M. Poiseuille (1840), C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 11:961-967, 1041-1048: the exact (Hagen-Poiseuille) solution of the Navier-Stokes equations for fully developed laminar pipe flow
reference.conditions: fully developed, steady, Newtonian; Re = rho U D / mu with U the bulk (mean) speed; Re = 100

quantities.label: Development length L_e / D (to 99 % of the developed centreline speed)
quantities.how: the first x where the centreline speed from Plot over path (0,0,0) to (0.3,0,0) m, 300 subdivisions, reaches 99 % of the same line's developed value (its mean over x/D 10 to 13), linearly interpolated between samples, over D_eff

reference.citation: F. Durst, S. Ray, B. Ünsal, O. A. Bayoumi (2005), "The development lengths of laminar pipe and channel flows", J. Fluids Eng. 127:1154-1160
reference.where: the pipe correlation L/D = [0.619^1.6 + (0.0567 Re)^1.6]^(1/1.6) (constants as quoted from the abstract by citing papers; error under 3 % for all laminar Re), 5.77 at Re 100
reference.conditions: laminar, uniform inlet; the distance to 99 % of the developed centreline velocity; Re = 100
reference.note: Depends on the 99 % definition and on the inlet profile; the 0.05 Re rule (5.0) is about 13 % short.
